title: A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory
abstract: arXiv:2611.02912v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-lived agents rely on persistent memory of users, tasks and decisions, and this memory must stay consistent with a world that keeps changing. When an upstream fact changes, however, memory systems can revise the contradicted memory itself while the beliefs, plans and actions derived from it remain accepted, even though they have lost their support. We therefore formulate dependency-aware state revision, which asks not only what changed but also which dependent states should no longer be trusted. To address it, StateGraph maintains an evolving state dependency graph whose edges are recovered from interaction histories. translated_title: 状态变化是局部的，其后果却不是：面向长期智能体记忆的依赖感知状态修订
translated_abstract: 长期运行的智能体依赖于关于用户、任务和决策的持久记忆，而这些记忆必须与不断变化的世界保持一致。然而，当上游事实发生变化时，记忆系统往往只会修订被矛盾的记忆本身，而由其推导出的信念、计划和行动仍然被保留，即使它们已经失去了支撑。因此，我们提出了依赖感知状态修订这一问题，它不仅关注什么发生了变化，还关注哪些依赖状态不应再被信任。为解决这一问题，StateGraph 维护一个不断演进的状态依赖图，其边从交互历史中恢复。其核心设计是反事实验证：每条候选边通过询问“如果失去其前提，依赖状态是否仍然成立”来进行检验，从而将支撑性依赖与语义相关性区分开来；修订过程仅在严格依赖失效且不存在独立支持的情况下才使依赖状态失效。
tldr: 提出依赖感知状态修订问题，并通过 StateGraph 从交互历史中恢复状态依赖图，利用反事实验证区分真实的支撑依赖与语义相关性，从而在上游事实变化时自动失效失去支撑的下游信念、计划和行动。
en_tdlr: The paper formulates dependency-aware state revision and introduces StateGraph, which recovers a state dependency graph from interaction histories and uses counterfactual verification to distinguish genuine support dependence from semantic relatedness, thereby invalidating dependent beliefs, plans, and actions that lose their support when upstream facts change.
